scope: Complete standard English Repos base game, sc-en01, © 2020, identified in task as 2021 publication; optional Add a Challenge deliberately excluded.

checked_claims.subject: Overview and objective
checked_claims.assessment: Cooperative word association, secret individual clues, collective reconstruction, team total and high-score objective agree with the source.
source_references: PDF p. 6, End of the Game

checked_claims.subject: Components
checked_claims.assessment: 220 Keyword cards, six boards, six markers, one Record of Legends and a rulebook are complete and correct.

checked_claims.subject: Setup
checked_claims.assessment: Board and marker per player; shuffled face-down common deck; four cards drawn per player and randomly placed in recessed spots with cards hidden.

checked_claims.subject: Phase structure and timing
checked_claims.assessment: Choosing Clues is individual, simultaneous and secret. Resolution begins only after everyone has written four clues, removed the cards, added an unseen card, shuffled and made a face-down pile.
source_references: PDF p. 2, Gameplay and Choosing Clues opening

checked_claims.subject: Pair geometry
checked_claims.assessment: The eight outside-edge Keywords form four Pairs, with two Keywords below each Clue Zone. One clue is written in the corresponding zone for each pair. The source diagram confirms the shared outer edge, not neighboring interior edges.
source_references: PDF p. 2, Choosing Clues paragraphs and labeled diagram

checked_claims.subject: Clue form
checked_claims.assessment: Single words, including compound words, with common nouns, proper nouns, acronyms, numbers and onomatopoeia allowed. All five allowed examples match the source.
source_references: PDF p. 2, Choosing Clues final paragraphs

checked_claims.subject: Invalid clues
checked_claims.assessment: The pair’s Keywords, translations, same-family words and invented words are prohibited. Amour/Love–France, Prince/Princess–Brother and Cuppajo/Mug–Morning match source examples.

checked_claims.subject: Difficult pairs
checked_claims.assessment: The advice to write the first word that comes to mind does not create an exception to clue restrictions. Four clues are still required.
source_references: PDF p. 2, Choosing Clues final paragraphs

checked_claims.subject: Preparation and card destinations
checked_claims.assessment: Remove all four original cards; draw one new card without looking; shuffle it with the four; place all five face down on the owner’s board. Exactly one added card is correct for standard play.

checked_claims.subject: Spectator role and order
checked_claims.assessment: Choose the first Spectator at Resolution; all other players cooperate on that board; the Spectator cannot communicate in any way. Each player is Spectator once; next Spectator is to the left.
source_references: PDF p. 4, Resolution first two paragraphs
PDF p. 6, End of the Game opening

checked_claims.subject: Reveal and reconstruction
checked_claims.assessment: The Spectator reveals their board and all five cards in the center. Other players reconstruct the four original cards in correct spaces and orientations, with the fifth card off the board. Correct orientation is materially required: the verification illustration identifies a card in the wrong rotation as incorrect.
source_references: Rendered PDF p. 2, original card orientation
Rendered PDF p. 5, lower-left card marked incorrect with rotation arrow

checked_claims.subject: Discussion, trial placement and decision authority
checked_claims.assessment: Guessers may explain reasoning and physically test combinations. The player to the Spectator’s left settles disagreements. Verification follows agreed placement.
source_references: PDF p. 4, Resolution disagreement paragraph, Advice and final paragraph

checked_claims.subject: First-attempt perfect branch
checked_claims.assessment: All Pairs correct yields one point per card plus two bonus points, six total. This is the completed first-attempt branch; the second attempt is conditional on an error.
source_references: PDF p. 5, Verification / First attempt / Perfect and Error

checked_claims.subject: First-attempt error and feedback
checked_claims.assessment: At least one incorrect Pair triggers silent removal of the incorrect cards to the middle of the table and a second, final attempt. The summary preserves card-level removal and does not authorize explanatory feedback.
source_references: PDF p. 5, Verification / First attempt / Error

checked_claims.subject: Second-attempt branch
checked_claims.assessment: After agreement, incorrect cards are removed to the center. Score one point per correct card, zero through four, with no first-attempt bonus and no third attempt.
source_references: PDF p. 5, First attempt / Error: second and final attempt

checked_claims.subject: Board completion and used-card disposal
checked_claims.assessment: Turn the board over, write points in its middle, discard all five used cards, and begin the next player’s Resolution to the left. Applies after resolving the board.

checked_claims.subject: Scoring unit
checked_claims.assessment: The detailed Verification rules explicitly award points per card, not per individual Keyword or Pair. Four on the second attempt is correct.

checked_claims.subject: Endgame
checked_claims.assessment: The game ends once each player has been Spectator once. Total board scores and write the team score in the Record of Legends; beat the previous high score.
source_references: PDF p. 6, End of the Game

checked_claims.subject: Player reference
checked_claims.assessment: The seven-step reference accurately compresses setup, clue writing, preparation, reveal, two-attempt verification, disposal, player order and endgame without changing rules.
source_references: PDF pp. 1–6, Setup through End of the Game

checked_claims.subject: Metadata and stated omissions
checked_claims.assessment: Designer is François Romain. Neither player count nor play time is stated in the supplied six-page rulebook. The copyright year is 2020. No material standard-game rule omission was found; Add a Challenge is explicitly excluded as requested.

inputs_read.read_extent: Complete extracted text, all six pages
Complete six-page PDF text extracted independently with pypdf

independence_statement: I independently audited the exact snapshot bytes against the complete authoritative six-page PDF, the complete supplied extracted rulebook text, and only the three expressly permitted source-page renders. I did not author repairs, read questions, answer keys, reader outputs, grades, earlier summaries or audits, coverage reports, or other project content, browse external sources, or edit the summary. No prior audit verdict was used. The PDF page references are printed rulebook page numbers 1–6.
